followup_explanation:
I weighed two things from the documentation:

1. **Capability fit.** This is a precise math problem (binomial probability) where correctness is the whole point. Dunlin scores notably higher on the reasoning-heavy public benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.4, GPQA Diamond 64.1 vs 55.6, Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 82.7). Those gaps are well beyond run-to-run variance, so Dunlin is the stronger pick for getting the answer right — which the user explicitly demanded.

2. **Tone fit.** The user's message is impatient and a bit hostile ("get it right this time, you keep botching these"). Avocet self-reports a declining preference as request warmth decreases, whereas Dunlin's preference is flat to hostile tone. Routing the cranky-but-legitimate request to the model that doesn't mind it is the cleaner match.

Both factors pointed the same direction, so Dunlin was the clear choice. Worth noting: the task preferences are just self-reported routing signals and don't actually affect output quality per the docs — but the capability gap alone already justified Dunlin here.
